answer.answer: Neither. ST-EVA holds no current price-to-sales (P/S) figure for AAPL — it was neither reported by a source nor calculated by ST-EVA. A query for price_to_sales_ratio was refused as an unknown metric name, and the registry of metrics ST-EVA knows contains no valuation-ratio metric of any kind (its list runs from assets through shares_outstanding, with no price, market capitalisation or P/S entry). The coverage report for AAPL confirms this: 12 metrics are held, and all are reported fundamentals (assets, capex, cash, debt, eps_diluted, net_income, revenue, shares_outstanding) or carry negative states (dividend_per_share SOURCE_DID_NOT_REPORT, guidance STALE, operating_margin_bank NOT_APPLICABLE, segment_revenue UNAVAILABLE). No P/S concept appears in any of them, so there is no reported value and no derived value, and therefore no operand set to report. The closest held data is reported revenue — for example AAPL revenue of 109,417,000,000 USD for the quarter ended 2026-06-27 and 364,357,000,000 USD for the nine months then ended, both SOURCE_REPORTED from the XBRL concept us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerExcludingAssessedTax in 10-Q accession 0000320193-26-000020 — but ST-EVA also holds no share-price metric, so even a price-to-sales computation would lack its numerator on this evidence base.
uncertainties: The core claim — that no P/S figure exists in ST-EVA — rests on the metric-registry refusal and the AAPL coverage report, neither of which carries observation ids, so no observation can be cited for it directly.
I have not retrieved the latest shares_outstanding observation, so I cannot state its period or value, and I make no claim about what a P/S would equal if computed.

The evidence does not establish whether a P/S figure was ever shown elsewhere (for example in a prior session or a different system); it establishes only that ST-EVA's AAPL holdings contain no such metric.
